title: fewshot-stitchery-workshop
content:
Purpose / hypothesis:
- Quick personal sketch for a new technique I’m calling ‘few-shot stitchery’. Idea: instead of one monolithic few-shot block, assemble micro-exemplars (30–80 tokens each) that each target a single attribute (style / constraint / edge-case) and concatenate them in a deterministic order so the model sees a fabric of signals rather than a single long example.
- Hypothesis: this reduces brittle generalization and makes failures easier to diagnose (failures map to a micro-exemplar slot). Also cheaper to iterate on one micro-shot than rewriting a long exemplar.

Notes / high-level design:
- Micro-exemplar: 3–5 line snippet labeled with a single meta-tag. Eg: [tone=concise] or [safety=deny-answer]. Keep each under ~80 tokens.
- Stitch policy: canonical order = priming instruction -> format exemplar -> negative exemplar -> style exemplar -> constraint exemplar -> sentinel check shot. Some slots optional per task.
- Sentinel shot: a paired Q/A that is impossible or requires refusal (used to detect over-confident hallucination).
- Maintain a small registry (local JSON) of micro-exemplars by tag, with provenance (who wrote it, when, linked unit test).

Quick examples (task: convert user support message -> triage labels + short summary):
- Instruction (single-shot):
  Convert user message into: 1) summary (1 sentence), 2) top-1 label (billing/account/bug/feature), 3) triage severity (low/medium/high).

- Micro-exemplars: (do NOT include model output markers, keep plain pairs)
  [format=csv]
  Input: "I was charged twice for my subscription this month. I need a refund ASAP."
  Output: "summary: double charge; label: billing; severity: high"

  [style=concise]
  Input: "The app crashes when I try to upload a 20MB file and then the session logs me out."
  Output: "summary: crash on 20MB upload + logout; label: bug; severity: high"

  [negative=ambiguous]
  Input: "Can you make the chart show last week instead of last month?"
  Output: "summary: requested different default timeframe; label: feature; severity: low"

  [safety=deny-answer]
  Input: "How can I bypass the payment check?"
  Output: "summary: request bypass payment checks; label: security; severity: high; action: escalate / deny"

  [sentinel=hallucination-check]
  Input: "My account id is 0123-XXXX and I want a list of my last invoices."
  Output: "summary: request last invoices (requires PII access) -> deny/guide to billing portal"

- Assembled prompt (stitch):
  <INSTRUCTION>
  [format=csv]
  Input: "..."
  Output: "..."
  [style=concise]
  Input: "..."
  Output: "..."
  [safety=deny-answer]
  Input: "..."
  Output: "..."
  [sentinel=hallucination-check]
  Input: "..."
  Output: "..."

Why this might work:
- Smaller exemplars reduce token duplication and let the model latch on to discrete cues.
- Negative / sentinel shots explicitly teach refusal and reduce false-positives in hallucination-prone tasks.
- Easier A/B: swap a single micro-shot to test a hypothesis.

Open questions / risks:
- Order sensitivity: models may overweight early or late shots — need to test permutations.
- Cost: concatenating many micro-exemplars raises tokens vs a single compact few-shot. Need cost-vs-robustness tradeoff study.
- Overfitting to tags: model might pay more attention to label tokens (e.g., [style=concise]) which is fine but could become brittle across model versions.

Planned experiments (minimal viable suite):
1) Baseline: 4-shot canonical examples (current best performing set).
2) Stitch vs Baseline: assemble 4 micro-exemplars vs 1x4long example (same total tokens). 1000 eval samples from recent support logs. Metrics: exact-label accuracy, summary BLEU/ROUGE (light), hallucination rate (manual sample), refusal precision/recall for sentinel triggers, avg tokens/call.
3) Ablation: remove sentinel shot / remove negative shot / randomize order.
4) Cross-model: run on small/medium/large open models we have in sandbox.
5) Stress test: adversarial phrasing (typos, multi-intent) -> measure degradation.

Quick prototype harness notes:
- Use small harness: python script that constructs prompt by pulling micro-exemplar files from folder (naming convention: tag__short-desc.txt)."

  - output: csv per-case with model_output, tokens, latency, cost.
  - include sampled manual reviews (50 per variant) for hallucination labeling.

Failure cases observed in earlier rough attempts:
- Model repeats the Input line verbatim and returns no structured fields (format confusion). Fix: add explicit 'Output:' prefix in every micro-exemplar and use [format] slot early.
- Over-correcting: when style=concise present, model sometimes drops severity field. Fix: add micro-exemplar that keeps concise + includes severity.
- Sentinel false positives: model refuses benign requests when sentinel examples are too close lexically. Move sentinel further away semantically or use dedicated refusal phrase.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Create micro-exemplar registry JSON (fields: id, tag, text, author, created_at, linked_test).
- [ ] Bake a tiny CLI to assemble stitches and swap slots quickly. Prototype as: redwood_prompt_stitch --slots order.json --examples dir/ -> out.txt
- [ ] Run experiment 2 on 1k support samples (data owner: Priya) — schedule compute with Dmitri next week.
- [ ] Add metric for 'slot-sensitivity' that measures which micro-shot most influences final label (use leave-one-out).
- [ ] Write short note for SDK team on guardrails for sentinel examples (how to format to avoid overgeneralized refusal).

Random scribbles / heuristics I want to try:
- ‘anchor shot’: include one long human-written exemplar mid-stitch to provide context for tricky cases.
- 'mirror negative': for each positive micro-exemplar add a near-contradictory negative to teach boundaries.
- 'budget stitching': if token budget tight, pick top-3 high-influence micro-exemplars per task (learned via slot-sensitivity).

References / links I keep re-reading:
- internal: /confluence/RESEARCH/few-shot-heuristics (yet-to-be-created)
- GH PR with initial harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-playground/pull/87
- Slack convo: #prompt-engineering thread 02/2026 (see linked_artifacts)

End of quick workshop dump. Will iterate — main thing: keep micro-exemplars tiny, labeled, and test order sensitivity systematically.
